### Understanding the Problem

The theorem states: "If a straight-line falling across two straight-lines makes the alternate angles equal to one another then the (two) straight-lines will be parallel to one another."

In geometry, this is a classic theorem about parallel lines. When a transversal (the "falling across" line) intersects two lines, if the alternate interior angles are equal, then the two lines are parallel.
